text:
Maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in duplicate accounts and users losing org roles since the IdP change at 03:10 UTC. Not sure if it's JIT or assertion differences.
Sahil: Confirmed in app logs: a bunch of `user_provision create` events with different subject_id values but same email. Looks like NameID changed.
Jen: I pulled three SAML assertions from the deploy window. Old NameID (persistent) vs new NameID (transient/pairwise) — different values for same principal.
Jen: ```
<Subject>
  <NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent">abc123:company</NameID>
</Subject>
---after migration---
<Subject>
  <NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient">def456:random</NameID>
</Subject>
```
Leo: Oof. Our JIT key is `subject_id` first, fall back to `email` only if subject absent — so rotation creates new user rows.
Sahil: Logs show `duplicate_user_created` 34x in the last 20m. Audit entries: event=user.create reason=subject_rotation, user.email=alice@example.com.
Maria: Can we flip JIT temporarily to check email first instead of subject? That would avoid creating duplicates while IdP fixes persistent-id.
Jen: Quick mitigation I propose: 1) Disable auto-provisioning for new users, 2) Run a dedupe script that links old subjects -> new subjects by email, 3) Re-enable JIT with a short TTL on new mappings.
security-oncall: Need an audit trail before we touch mappings. Please grab org.audit_logs for the last 48h (SAML assertions + provisioning events) and stash into S3 encrypted with customer KMS key. Pin the S3 object name.
okta-bot: provisioning.event user=alice@example.com action=create subject_id=def456 source=okta ts=1786501180
okta-bot: provisioning.event user=alice@example.com action=create subject_id=ghi789 source=okta ts=1786501195
Sahil: Proposed dedupe SQL (dry-run first):
```sql
-- find potential duplicates by email where multiple subject_ids exist
SELECT email, array_agg(subject_id) FROM users WHERE email IN (SELECT email FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING count(distinct subject_id) > 1) GROUP BY email;
-- link new subject to existing account (example)
UPDATE subjects SET user_id = u.id FROM users u WHERE subjects.subject_id = 'def456' AND u.email = 'alice@example.com';
```
Jen: We'll need to be careful: some customers intentionally use pairwise NameIDs. Put a flag to skip dedupe for tenants with `require_nameid_persistent=true`.
Leo: Also check role assignment logic — we saw a case where missing `department` attribute caused fallback to org-admin role. Could cause privilege escalation if dedupe picks wrong account.
Maria: Good catch. For safety: while dedupe runs, also temporarily lock role changes for deduped accounts (no auto-admin grants).
security-oncall: I'll pull the audit logs now and hand off a signed copy. Also request: contact IdP SRE to confirm whether persistent-id rotation was intentional. If intentional, we'll schedule a migration doc.
Sahil: Plan for an 11:30 UTC maintenance window to: disable JIT autoprovision, run dedupe dry-run, run actual dedupe, enable JIT with email-first fallback for 24h, verify metrics.
Jen: I'll draft the runbook and post to #incidents. Include rollback: re-enable previous JIT behavior and recreate any missing subject mappings from the audit bundle.
Maria: Thanks — assign owners: Sahil (executes dedupe), Jen (runbook + run coord), Leo (role-safety checks), security-oncall (audit package + IdP contact).
Leo: I'll add quick invariant checks: no account should gain admin role during window, and no token issued with new subject before mapping.
Maria: Emoji vote: thumbs? :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:
Sahil: :thumbsup:
Jen: :thumbsup:
Leo: :thumbsup:
security-oncall: :thumbsup:
Maria: I'll start a postmortem ticket and label it `sso/jit-persistentid-rotation`. Keep chat updates brief in the incident thread.
